seoTitle: Crucible for Plex: a native Plex client for iPhone, iPad and Apple TV
metaDescription: Crucible is a free, open-source Plex client for iPhone, iPad and Apple TV on the App Store: a Resume-first Home, Skip Intro, playback that keeps your place, offline downloads, an iPad app with windows and keyboard shortcuts, a Liquid Glass tvOS app, a Year in Review dashboard and a built-in demo. Optional Crucible Pro, once or yearly.
keywords: plex resume where you left off
heroHeadline: Plex, done right on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV
heroSubhead: A fast, native Plex client for iPhone and iPad and a Liquid Glass living-room app for Apple TV, on one engine: a Resume-first Home, Skip Intro, playback that keeps your place through sleep and breaks, a Year in Review of your viewing and menus that look like the system's own. Free on the App Store, open source, and there is a built-in demo if you have no server to hand.
highlights: Free on the App Store for iPhone, iPad and Apple TV, with an optional Crucible Pro that covers all three
A Resume-first Home on every device: Continue Watching and Up Next lead, the artwork does the rest
iPad: a library sidebar, several windows, a menu bar and keyboard shortcuts, with layouts that use a large window
Apple TV: a cinematic Home, the system player, native menus and Top Shelf
iPhone: offline downloads with a Live Activity, Skip Intro, Picture-in-Picture and background audio
Keeps your place: back at the exact moment you left after sleep, a short rewind after a break, and Still watching? before a season plays on
Open source under GPL-3.0, with no account, ads or analytics: it talks only to plex.tv and your server

features.title: Made for the couch
features.body: On Apple TV a full-screen backdrop follows focus, the hero shows the title, details and synopsis, and rails of Continue Watching, Up Next and Recently Added sit under it. Select opens, Play/Pause plays, a long press opens a native context menu. Liquid Glass controls on tvOS 26, the classic look with the same layout on older systems.

features.title: Made for iPad
features.body: Crucible is one universal app, so the iPad runs the same app with room to spread out. A sidebar lists your libraries, and several windows can be open at once: choose Open in New Window on a title, or drag its card to the edge of the screen. A menu bar and keyboard shortcuts cover the rest (Space plays, S skips the intro or credits, N plays the next episode, Command-F searches), artwork lifts under the pointer, and rails, grids and detail pages use the room a large window gives them. One Crucible Pro purchase covers iPhone, iPad and Apple TV.

features.title: A player that respects your time
features.body: Skip Intro and Skip Credits from Plex markers — on iPhone as a button with a live progress sweep, automatic with Undo, or off; on Apple TV as native actions on the system player, with an Up Next card that counts down to the next episode. Picture-in-Picture, background audio and lock-screen controls come along on iPhone. On Apple TV you choose how far a click left or right on the remote skips, and whether holding either side rewinds and fast-forwards as usual, jumps 1 to 10 minutes, starts over or plays the next episode; on iPhone the same distances drive the Lock Screen, Control Center and headphone skip buttons.

features.title: Keeps your place
features.body: If the Apple TV sleeps, the app goes to the background or the server drops the stream while you are away, Crucible puts you back at the exact moment you left: it never restarts the episode or skips ahead. Come back after a break and playback backs up a few seconds, more the longer you were gone, so you are back in the scene; Settings can turn that off. After a few episodes in a row without touching the remote, Crucible asks Still watching? before the next one, so a season does not play on while you sleep: off, or after 2, 3 or 5 episodes, 3 by default.

features.title: Take it offline
features.body: Download movies, whole seasons or single episodes at the quality you pick, from Original to Data Saver, or let a season sheet grab the unwatched or the next three. Downloads run in the background, resume on their own and stay Wi-Fi-only unless you say otherwise, with a Live Activity on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island. One download at a time is free; Crucible Pro lifts the limit.

features.title: Plays anything, your way
features.body: Direct play when your device handles the file, automatic HLS transcoding through Plex's universal transcoder when it doesn't. Subtitle and audio track selection, adjustable speed, cast and crew, and More Like This on every title.

features.title: Browse the way you think
features.body: Home opens on a Resume hero, then Continue Watching, Up Next and Recently Added. Every library has filter chips for Unwatched and In Progress, genre and sort, an A–Z scrubber, a Recently Watched rail and raw folder browsing, and search groups results by type with a Top Result. On Apple TV each movie or show library gets its own tab.

features.title: Try it without a server
features.body: No Plex server yet? Choose Try the demo on the welcome screen and explore a fictional library with everything unlocked: Home, search, playback with Skip Intro, Statistics and, on iPhone, downloads and the Year in Review poster. A short guided tour shows each part, and leaving the demo takes you to the real Plex sign-in.

features.title: Know your viewing
features.body: Watch History grouped by day and a Year-in-Review dashboard of watch time, streaks, an activity heatmap, top shows, binges and taste, built from your own Plex history on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV. The last week is free; Crucible Pro adds the month, year and all-time views, the library filter and the shareable poster.

features.title: Continues across devices
features.body: Watch progress syncs to your server, so Resume picks up where you left off on your phone, your iPad, your TV or anywhere else you sign in. Handoff and Spotlight carry titles between your Apple devices, and the Apple TV signs in from your phone with a short code and a QR code.

features.title: Built different
features.body: Swift 6 and programmatic UIKit, with one shared engine under both apps: networking, playback, statistics and every screen's rules are shared, and the screens only render them. Liquid Glass, Light and Dark, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver throughout. It is open source, and the iPhone app is cross-compiled on Arch Linux and deployed over USB with no Xcode and no macOS; the Apple TV app is an Xcode project.

howItWorks.step: Get it on the App Store
howItWorks.body: Crucible for Plex is one free listing for iPhone, iPad and Apple TV. No server yet? Open it and choose Try the demo.

Authenticate with Plex over OAuth on iPhone and iPad, or with a short code and QR code from your phone on Apple TV. Crucible discovers your servers and picks the best reachable connection automatically.

Pick up with the Resume hero, filter your poster grids or search everything you own, then direct play or transcode, skip the intro, send it to Picture-in-Picture and let Up Next roll the next episode.

faq.q: Is Crucible on the App Store?
faq.a: Yes. Crucible for Plex is a free download on the App Store, one listing for iPhone, iPad and Apple TV. It is also open source under GPL-3.0, so you can build it yourself if you prefer; a build from source is fully unlocked.

faq.q: What is free, and what is Crucible Pro?
faq.a: Browsing, search and playback are free on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV, with Skip Intro, Skip Credits, Picture-in-Picture on iPhone, the Statistics view for the last week and one download at a time. Crucible Pro unlocks unlimited offline downloads, the full Statistics screen with every range and library filter, the Year in Review poster and Top Shelf on Apple TV. Pay once for lifetime access or subscribe yearly with a 14-day free trial; one purchase covers iPhone, iPad and Apple TV, and Family Sharing is on.

faq.q: Can I try it without a Plex server?
faq.a: Yes. Choose Try the demo on the welcome screen. It runs a fictional library from inside the app, with no account and no network, and everything is unlocked so you can try playback, search, Statistics and, on iPhone, downloads. A short tour walks you through it, and leaving the demo takes you to the real Plex sign-in.

Yes. Crucible is a universal app, so the iPad uses the same App Store listing and the same Crucible Pro purchase as the iPhone. On a large window it uses the room: a sidebar lists your libraries, you can open several windows (Open in New Window on a title, or drag its card to the edge of the screen), a menu bar and keyboard shortcuts cover the common actions (Space plays, S skips the intro or credits, N plays the next episode, Command-F searches), and artwork lifts under the pointer. A narrow window, Split View or Slide Over looks like the phone. It runs on iPadOS 17 or later; the library sidebar needs iPadOS 18 and the menu bar iPadOS 26.

faq.q: Is there an Apple TV app?
faq.a: Yes, in the same App Store listing as the iPhone app. It is built for the Siri Remote on the same engine: a cinematic Home, a tab for every library, search, movie, show and episode pages, the system player with Skip Intro and Skip Credits as native actions and an Up Next card, Watch History, Statistics, a Year in Review card and a Top Shelf extension. It runs on tvOS 17 or later; tvOS 26 on an Apple TV 4K (2nd generation or later) gets Liquid Glass controls, and older systems and boxes get the classic look with the same layout.

faq.q: What happens if playback is interrupted, or I fall asleep?
faq.a: Crucible keeps your place. If the Apple TV sleeps, the app goes to the background or the server drops the stream while you are away, it puts you back at the exact moment you left and never restarts the episode or skips ahead. After a break, playback backs up a few seconds (more the longer you were away) so you are back in the scene; you can turn that off in Settings. After a few episodes in a row without touching the remote, Crucible asks Still watching? before it plays the next one. Settings lets you turn that off or ask after 2, 3 or 5 episodes; the default is 3.

Not on your home network. To stream away from home, Plex asks for a Plex Pass on the server owner's account or a Remote Watch Pass on yours, and Skip Intro and Skip Credits rely on markers that a Plex Pass server detects. Those are Plex's rules, not Crucible's, and they can change. Crucible is an independent app and is not made by, endorsed by or affiliated with Plex, Inc.

faq.q: What does it need to run?
faq.a: An iPhone on iOS 17 or later, an iPad on iPadOS 17 or later or an Apple TV on tvOS 17 or later, and a Plex Media Server you can reach. Crucible talks directly to your server, so a device away from home needs a route to it; it works well over Tailscale.

faq.q: Does it support Skip Intro, PiP, and lock-screen controls?
faq.a: Yes, and they are free. Skip Intro and Skip Credits come from Plex chapter markers, on iPhone and on Apple TV. On iPhone, Picture-in-Picture and background audio keep playback going and the lock screen and Control Center drive play, skip, scrub, and next episode. On Apple TV they are native actions on the system player.

faq.q: Can I download movies and shows to watch offline?
faq.a: Yes, on iPhone. Download movies, full seasons, or single episodes at the quality you choose, from Original to Data Saver. Downloads run in the background and resume after interruptions, stay Wi-Fi-only unless you allow cellular, and live in a Downloads tab with a storage summary, the live queue and one-tap cleanup of watched titles. A Live Activity shows progress on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island. One download at a time is free; Crucible Pro removes the limit. Offline playback uses the same player, so Skip Intro and Credits, resume and Picture-in-Picture all work with no network.

faq.q: Can I leave a library out of Home and my statistics?
faq.a: Yes. Settings › Libraries has a switch for each library, and the Statistics screen has the same switches in a filter menu, which is part of Crucible Pro. Libraries you've hidden from Home in Plex start switched off, and at least one library always stays on.

Yes: GPL-3.0, with one third-party dependency for the statistics store (GRDB) and pure Apple frameworks for everything else; the App Store build adds RevenueCat for purchases. Read the code, file an issue, or fork it on GitHub.

Yes. The iPhone app builds with xtool on Linux, Windows (WSL) or a Mac, with no Xcode interface needed, and is installed over USB with your own Apple ID; a free Apple ID's build stops opening after seven days, a paid account lasts a year. The Apple TV app needs a Mac with Xcode 26 or newer and XcodeGen, because xtool doesn't support tvOS. A build from source has no Pro purchase and nothing locked. The steps are below.

install.title: Or build it from source,
install.intro: Crucible is open source, so you can build it yourself instead of using the App Store: the iPhone app once with xtool, signed with your own Apple ID, over USB (a free Apple ID is enough); the Apple TV app with Xcode on a Mac. A build from source is fully unlocked, with no Pro purchase. You need an iPhone on iOS 17 or later, a cable, and a Mac, a Linux PC, or Windows with WSL.

steps.title: Install xtool
steps.body: xtool builds and installs iOS apps without Xcode's interface. On a Mac, install Xcode 26 or newer from the App Store, open it once, then install xtool.
steps.note: On Linux or Windows (WSL) you install Swift 6.4, usbmuxd, and Xcode's `.xip` from Apple instead; the step-by-step guide below lists each command.

steps.title: Sign in to Apple
steps.body: Pick `1: Password` to use any Apple ID, a free one included, then enter the two-factor code. Your credentials go only to Apple. On Linux and Windows it also asks for the path to the `.xip`.

steps.title: Build it and put it on your phone
steps.body: Plug the phone in, unlock it and tap Trust. The script checks your setup, builds Crucible in release mode and installs it. The first build takes several minutes. If it asks for Developer Mode, turn it on in Settings > Privacy & Security, restart the phone and run the script again.

steps.title: Trust it and open it
steps.body: On the phone: Settings > General > VPN & Device Management > your Apple ID > Trust, then open Crucible and sign in with Plex. A free Apple ID's build stops opening after 7 days; run the script again to renew it.

steps.title: Apple TV, optional
steps.body: The Apple TV app is an Xcode project, because xtool doesn't support tvOS. It needs a Mac with Xcode 26 or newer and XcodeGen. Generate the project, open it, choose your signing team and run it on your paired Apple TV; the README and `tv/README.md` cover the details.
code: cd Crucible/tv && xcodegen generate && open CrucibleTV.xcodeproj
steps.note: The Top Shelf extension needs the App Group capability, so it only shows up when your signing setup provides it. tvOS 17 or later; Liquid Glass needs tvOS 26 on an Apple TV 4K (2nd generation) or later.

tiers.note: once, never renews; launch price, rising to $24.99 on December 7, 2026

pricing.footnote: Prices are US dollars and vary by region. The annual subscription renews automatically until cancelled in your Apple Account settings, at least 24 hours before the end of the period; the lifetime unlock never renews. Both are family-shareable, and either one unlocks Crucible Pro on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV. A build from source is always fully unlocked.

trustNote: Crucible has no account of its own, no ads and no analytics. It talks only to plex.tv and the server you choose; the only third-party service is RevenueCat, which validates purchases.
